description:
## Goal

After fz-5xp.30 lands the truthful private-extern/total-arithmetic cutover, make the existing runtime export inventory the complete physical calling-contract and registration authority. A user can privately declare a runtime-owned symbol; a mismatch must be rejected before an unsafe call or an optimized substitution.

Source declarations own Fz semantic types, correlations and ordinary callable identity. The manifest owns real export name, ABI, fixed/variadic calling shape, physical scalar/aggregate layout and registration. Do not turn the manifest into an intrinsic registry or another semantic/effect authority.

## Predecessor contract

fz-5xp.30 provides real exports, defp-only foreign declarations, typed identities, raw boolean = uint64_t 0/1, and fixed two-field scalar tuple C returns adapted into EXISTING Fz return lanes. Example: `extern "C" defp fz_op_add_ii(integer, integer) :: {integer, boolean}` matches a by-value C struct `{int64_t value; uint64_t failed;}`. Real arithmetic exports are total; Kernel failure branches call one `arithmetic_error/0 -> panic(:badarith)` helper. Native may replace validated resolved calls with equivalent CLIF arithmetic; interpreter calls the actual export.

.30 must already validate its new/changed exports safely. This ticket completes the inventory across the entire runtime and deletes partial/duplicate validation. Do not defer safety of any newly introduced unsafe call until this ticket, or introduce a second temporary manifest.

## Strategy

1. Inspect src/extern_contract.rs RUNTIME_SYMBOLS, runtime export declarations/registration, src/ir_codegen/runtime_syms.rs, interpreter symbol dispatch and the shared extern signature producer. Work from actual physical exports; compare the predecessor diff and current code rather than historic counts.
2. Extend/derive the ONE existing manifest representation so each runtime-owned export has its exact ABI and complete signature. Keep target-independent field types/order distinct from the target's physical C ABI classification.
3. At the common resolved declaration boundary validate ABI, fixed/variadic arity, scalar widths/banks, and aggregate field order/types/layout. Fz boolean is the predecessor's explicit word boolean, not C _Bool. Do not reduce aggregates to Any or validate only the count of flattened source fields.
4. Ensure interpreter, JIT and AOT resolve/register the same physical export. A native optimization is eligible only after that same validation; it cannot conceal an invalid declaration or a missing real implementation.
5. Keep other libraries open-world with normal supported-shape validation. Do not ban ordinary private libc/user-library externs or conflate declared semantic narrowing with a physical mismatch. Library selection belongs to fz-5xp.61.
6. Remove partial ABI tables/checks and platform-accidental dlsym success paths once the complete inventory replaces them. Preserve one physical lookup/address-registration mechanism; no global scan on warm compiler requests.

## Acceptance

- RED tests with exact, truthful native fixtures and deliberate runtime-owned declaration mismatches: wrong ABI/process parameter, wrong arity, float-vs-integer bank, boolean width/representation, scalar-vs-aggregate return, and swapped word/float fields. All doors reject before execution/substitution; test a real exported symbol rather than merely an unresolvable name.
- Correct source aliases and narrowed semantic contracts retain the declared physical ABI; local shadowed functions do not become optimizer intrinsics through their names.
- Correct scalar/boolean/aggregate runtime declarations and an ordinary non-runtime library call succeed on interpreter/JIT/AOT and supported target ABIs. Reuse .30's aggregate fixtures; .37 owns completing the older argument-shape matrix.
- Negative ABI tests are durable behavior/safety tests, not one-shot source-text migration scans. Keep them. Do not test calling a real C function through an intentionally wrong prototype.
- Same input reuses existing World/ProductMemo products; unrelated edits initiate no requested-root export scan or work. Exact manifest/product movement invalidates only actual dependents.
- Update .agent/docs/externs.md, semantic-authorities.md and guides/externs.html to describe source-vs-physical authority and the final supported C layouts. Full relevant library/fixture/CLI/AOT tests, formatting, strict Clippy and workspace gates pass.

## Order and scope

Dependency: fz-5xp.30 -> this ticket -> fz-5xp.20, fz-kdt.28, fz-5xp.37. The three successors are independent follow-ons after the physical boundary is closed: wrapper inlining, proper exceptions at the shared arithmetic helper, and remaining extern coverage. They do not block this ticket.

Closed fz-5xp.29 is a rejected architecture, not an implementation prerequisite. No intrinsic syntax or semantic descriptor from it returns. Larger/nested aggregates, aggregate arguments, arrays/unions and public extern policy remain later API expansion, not prerequisites for validating the supported shapes.

Before starting, discuss this ticket's verified facts/plan as requested by the user. Use TDD and existing patterns. A fresh cold Sol-high ticket-scoped review precedes one commit/close and prompt push to the correct gh stack; Astra requires explicit permission.
title: Validate every runtime-owned extern against one exact physical ABI manifest
